### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in replacement; a string literal in semantic))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in replacement; a string literal in semantic))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in replacement; a string literal in semantic))_

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in replacement; a string literal in semantic))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 40d6c5fbd39db70f0e0885c046a11bef37baa0d9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8b7f00e27eb04a3016a2c31d06d84e2724ee66d1` — the merge of head `47c76064d73aa96d19046b36f4d1e9cddc63b29b` into base `40d6c5fbd39db70f0e0885c046a11bef37baa0d9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8b7f00e27eb04a3016a2c31d06d84e2724ee66d1 && git checkout 8b7f00e27eb04a3016a2c31d06d84e2724ee66d1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 40d6c5fbd39db70f0e0885c046a11bef37baa0d9 47c76064d73aa96d19046b36f4d1e9cddc63b29b && git checkout -B drift-repro 40d6c5fbd39db70f0e0885c046a11bef37baa0d9 && git merge --no-ff 47c76064d73aa96d19046b36f4d1e9cddc63b29b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 40d6c5fbd39db70f0e0885c046a11bef37baa0d9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 40d6c5fbd39db70f0e0885c046a11bef37baa0d9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `47c76064d73aa96d19046b36f4d1e9cddc63b29b`
Local-runs: none

Read-only shape held. Inputs: card #20831 (body and all three comments — triage 5908917971, claim 5910072345, os-dev-report 5911558951), PR #20856 (body, the 7-file list, `git diff origin/main...refs/review/pr20856` with `origin/main` at `40d6c5fbd`), the head's check-runs, and every factual claim re-read against `origin/main` and the objectui pin `db11afd49` (`.objectui-sha` on `origin/main`) with `git show` / `git grep`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on `47c76064d`, as read by this act (2026-09-30T12:57Z):** 30 `success` — among them the required `Lint & Repo Gates` (which runs `Migration registry matches its entry files`), `TypeScript Type Check` (the rollup; its four lanes `Type Check · source gates` with `check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs`, `check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide`, `check:export-origins`; `Type Check · consumer gates` with `check:api-surface`, `check:exported-any`; `Type Check · workspace`; `Type Check · debt ledger` — all `success`), `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and its three shards, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`; plus `Check Changeset` (the job that runs both `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major`), `Spec property liveness`, `Build Docs`, `Test Core (1/6)` to `(4/6)`; 2 `skipped` by design (`Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`); 2 still `in_progress` at the read: `Test Core (5/6)` and `(6/6)`. No check reads `failure`. The required `Test Core` rollup is therefore not final yet; this record judges the diff, and the landing waits on that conclusion as the queue rule already requires.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named and judged:

1. **`ComponentPropsMap['object-grid'].grouping`: `z.unknown()` to `GroupingConfigSchema.optional()` by reference — RIGHT.** On `origin/main` the row reads `grouping: z.unknown().optional().describe('Row grouping config')` (`component.zod.ts:3596`). `GroupingConfigSchema` (`view.zod.ts:1399`) is `strictObject({ fields: z.array(GroupingFieldSchema).min(1) })`; `GroupingFieldSchema` (`:1314`) carries the non-padded `field` superRefine (`checkGroupingFieldName`, `:1205`), `order` as an enum defaulting `asc`, `collapsed` as a boolean defaulting `false`. The narrowing is exactly the accept set `list-view` already applies, in the same `GroupingConfigSchema.optional().describe(...)` spelling (`view.zod.ts:2710`). The describe is kept. The renderer reads the whole shape: at the pin, `packages/types/src/objectql.ts:1123` types `grouping?: GroupingConfig` ("Aligned with @objectstack/spec GroupingConfigSchema"), `ObjectGrid.tsx:2050` and `:2839` read `schema.grouping?.fields`, and `useGroupedData.ts` reads `.field` / `.order` / `.collapsed` per entry (`:431-457`, `:490-517`). Triage's direction — type both rows, one schema, not a copy — is met.
2. **`ComponentPropsMap['object-kanban'].grouping`: the same change — RIGHT.** `origin/main` `component.zod.ts:3993` read `z.unknown()`. At the pin, `ObjectKanban.tsx:1211-1212` reads `schema.swimlaneField || (schema.grouping?.fields?.[0]?.field)` and nothing else of `grouping`. A `git grep` over objectui `packages/*/src` (tests excluded) at the pin for any `grouping.MEMBER` read other than `fields` returns 0 hits, so no renderer reads a member the typed shape would refuse. Typed, not retired, as triage ruled.
3. **Five refusal classes now reach both doors — RIGHT, and pinned with code AND path on both rows** (`component-object-block-grouping.pin.test.ts` §1: padded name `custom` at `grouping.fields.0.field`; non-object `invalid_type` at `grouping`; bare string `invalid_type` at `grouping`; `fields: []` `too_small` at `grouping.fields`; undeclared key inside the config `unrecognized_keys` at `grouping`). The message assertions (the received `"  business_unit  "`, then `Write "business_unit".`) match `checkGroupingFieldName`'s text on `origin/main` (`view.zod.ts:1209-1219`). Triage's second pin (a valid grouping parses byte-identical) is §2's `toStrictEqual` control; absence stays absence; §3 pins identity (`member.unwrap()._zod.def` is `GroupingConfigSchema._zod.def`) and corpus parity one path level down — the pin that reds a later copy of the shape, which triage forbade.
4. **Parse OUTPUT of a short-form entry `{ field }` now gains `order: 'asc'` and `collapsed: false` — RIGHT, and bounded.** It is the list view's existing behaviour, and nothing downstream consumes the output of these two rows: `PageComponentSchema.properties` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` on `origin/main` (`page.zod.ts:324`), so page parsing never applies the props schema; the only non-spec consumers of `ComponentPropsMap` are `@objectstack/lint` (`validate-component-props.ts` calls `safeParse` and reads issues only; `page-envelope-audit.ts` and `validate-page-field-bindings.ts` never call `.parse` nor read `.data`) and `sdui-parser`'s `kanban-quick-add.ts` (the retired `quickAdd` key, unrelated). Pinned as the short-form control.
5. **The published JSON Schemas for `ui/ObjectGridProps` and `ui/ObjectKanbanProps` now describe `grouping`'s shape — RIGHT, with no artifact left stale.** `json-schema.manifest/ui.json` lists schema NAMES only (both already listed); `authorable-surface/ui.json` records `Schema:key` rows only (`ui/ObjectGridProps:grouping` and `ui/ObjectKanbanProps:grouping` are already present on `origin/main`); `api-surface/` records export existence, and no export moved. `check:authorable-surface` (source gates) and `check:api-surface` (consumer gates) read `success`.
6. **`dropped-refinements.baseline.json`: two new sites (`grouping.fields.element.field` on both rows), `droppedRefinementSites` 610 to 612 — RIGHT.** The refinement is `GroupingFieldSchema`'s superRefine, which JSON Schema cannot express; `origin/main` already records the identical site on every list-view door (`ui/ListView`, `ui/ObjectListView`, `ui/GroupingConfig` as `fields.element.field`, and the manifest / `listViews` projections). Two sites, two lines, the count moved by exactly two. `refinementSitesThatDidProject` (369) is rightly untouched: the diff adds no projected site.
7. **`content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx` regenerated by `gen:docs` (both rows now `{ fields: object[] }` plus one Nested Shape table each) — RIGHT** (an AUTO-GEN surface, not hand-edited; `check:docs` and `Build Docs` green).
8. **ADR-0087 disposition `registered ui-object-block-grouping-config-typed`, a protocol-18 semantic entry and no D2 conversion — RIGHT.** Triage ruled "refused with guidance naming the field, never silently trimmed"; a trimming conversion would be the consumer tolerance Prime Directive #12 refuses. The entry's rewrite table (padded to unpadded; bare string wrapped; number / empty list / other deleted; `swimlaneField` wins on kanban) matches the changeset's table. The at-rest claim is verified (item 4), and the component-props rule is `tier: 'advisory'`, `surfaces: CLI_ONLY` on `origin/main` (`authoring-rules.ts:1022-1030`), so "a stored page keeps loading; the refusal reaches authors on `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint`" is a true statement. `registry.ts`: the emitted block is byte-identical to the entry file and sits in derived order (ids sorted within major 18 — after `ui-mcp-connect-agent-unknown-keys-refused`, before `ui-object-grid-page-size-positive-integer-refused`); the registry gate ran green inside `Lint & Repo Gates`. `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` is rightly unmoved: it renders majors up to `PROTOCOL_MAJOR` = 17 (`PROTOCOL_VERSION` is `17.0.0`), and step 18 is the unreleased next major (`check:upgrade-guide` green).
9. **`component.zod.ts` gains one import (`GroupingConfigSchema` from `./view.zod`) — RIGHT,** the only way to reference rather than copy; `view.zod.ts` imports nothing from `component.zod.ts`, and that import list already carried six lazy schemas, so no cycle is introduced.
10. **Consumer radius — RIGHT.** `examples/**` has 0 `object-kanban` nodes on `origin/main`, no spec UI test asserts `grouping` on these rows, and `@objectstack/lint` is the consumer that parses them (`Type Check · consumer gates` green).
11. **Unchanged, and rightly so:** `swimlaneField` semantics on kanban; `ListView.grouping`; `GroupingConfigSchema` itself and its exports.

Residual, not a defect of this diff: the section header at `component.zod.ts:3315-3316` still describes "filter shapes … grouping configs" as living in objectui — historical text, now stale for both; the dev noted it; a later tidy, not this narrowing.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/20831-object-block-grouping-typed.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, a **BREAKING** banner, the FROM-to-TO migration table with a one-line fix per refused shape, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, and exactly one marker `adr-0087: registered ui-object-block-grouping-config-typed`. This matches what the diff publishes: an accept-set narrowing on two published props schemas of a released package. Under the declaration grammar, `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and takes `minor` with its migration (`check-changeset-no-major` admits no `major`); it is the grade triage gave ("a BREAKING `minor` line"). `Check Changeset` (both gates) reads `success` on this head. Neither `skip-changeset` nor `patch` — right.
- `Clause-②:` line. The claim (5910072345) and the PR body carry `Clause-②: yes`; the changeset carries `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. Value and level agree across all three carriers and the level axis is green. Precision reading against the criterion 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」: this diff widens no accept set and adds no export or key, so the literal spelling is `no (narrowing)`; `yes` over-declares the widening half (the reader's own docblock labels `yes (narrowing)` a diff that widens AND narrows). It under-declares nothing: the breaking fact rides the arm in the changeset, where `check-adr-0087-registration` reads it. Ruled under ③.
- The PR body's line carries no arm. Nothing reads the body's arm (the level gate reads the value; the ADR-0087 gate reads the changeset), so this is harmless; one spelling across the carriers is preferable if the seat touches the line.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev-declared deviations (6):

1. File-surface breach, `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` — **ACCEPTED.** The spec build refuses the schema change until the hand-edited ledger records the site; dropping the refinement is forbidden by the ledger's own rule, and teaching the projection a named pattern is a separate contract decision. Judged right in ①.6; declared, minimal (two parity lines), proportionate.
2. One import line outside "the two `grouping` members only" — **ACCEPTED** (①.9).
3. Triage's `grouping.fields[0].field` path for `grouping: 42` — **ACCEPTED as measured.** A number has no `fields[0]` to fail at; `invalid_type` at `grouping` is the correct issue, and the padded case carries triage's path on both rows.
4. Changeset `yes (narrowing)` beside the body's bare `yes` — **ACCEPTED**; see the open question.
5. `origin/main` merged through `os-regen-merge.sh` before the PR opened, zero regeneration diff — **ACCEPTED** (the prescribed sequence).
6. Model-free commit trailer pair per AGENTS.md rather than the harness reminder's — **ACCEPTED**; AGENTS.md outranks the reminder.

Open question — Clause-② value (A: keep `yes` / `yes (narrowing)` as graded; B: respell `no (narrowing)`): **answered, A stands for this head.** The value was graded by triage and executed by the claim; both gates read the same level (`minor`) and the same breaking arm under either spelling, and a narrowing declared `yes` is never under-declared. The precise literal spelling is B, and the line is the seat's (the claim's), not the dev's: if the seat respells, it respells all three carriers — claim, PR body, changeset — in one act before enqueue, so the carriers never disagree. No push is required by this record.

Out-of-scope findings (4, dev-noted, carrier none or the mirror card):

- `ui-object-grid-page-size-positive-integer-refused` says a stored page "is refused on its next authoring-path save", while its sibling entry and the rule registration (`tier: 'advisory'`, `surfaces: CLI_ONLY`) say advisory CLI only — **ESCALATED to the seat.** This is a sentence in shipped `os migrate meta` guidance; if the save path does not refuse, a machine-readable surface lies (Prime Directive #10). The seat measures one save and files a card if the reading holds. Not this PR's text.
- `refinementSitesThatDidProject` 369 recorded against 421 printed — pre-existing and ungated; **noted**, no action on this PR.
- The `component.zod.ts` section-header text — **noted** (① residual).
- objectui `plugin-kanban/src/index.tsx:684` and the `structuredKeysAreDeclaredAndHonoured-8313` test header describe the spec row as `z.unknown()` — **routed to the objectui mirror card** the seat files at ACCEPT (`Blocked-by:` this card), as triage directed; its row-4 fixture `{ fields: [{ field: 'owner' }] }` stays valid under the typed row.

No governed surface is touched (7 files under `.changeset/`, `content/docs/references/`, `packages/spec/`); the PR is draft, no auto-merge, no reviewer requested — the landing is the seat's after the required rollups conclude.

**VERDICT: PASS**
